title: session-record v1
description: The record Horde's engine STORES for one session, keyed by sessionId: the fields core/ownership.json gives to the engine and does not mark derived, and nothing else. A field another owner holds (agent, host, session) lives in that owner's store, and a derived field is computed when it is read; a stored copy of either would be a second writer, which step 0.6 forbids. Values are plain and typed: the engine writes facts it knows, and a field it has not set is absent - never an empty string, -1 or null standing in for 'none'. The answer-per-field VIEW of a session, over every owner, with unknowns, provenance and provisional marks, is a separate schema, session-view, deferred to step 2.3 where `horde status --json` produces it; the review's findings about value types and answer consistency (the tristate form) apply to that view, not to this record. test/test-schema-session-record.ps1 computes the field list from the ownership table and fails if the two ever differ.

sessionId.description: THE KEY, not a stored fact: the agent's own conversation id, which names this record. The agent owns it (core/ownership.json); the engine only files the record under it. Same shape as schema/pane-session.v1's session_id.

projectCwd.x-horde-read: W1 firstCwd, then X1 cwd, then W1 cwd
projectCwd.description: The directory the session was launched in, which names its transcript's project folder; fixed at start and never revised (wezfleet Write-WfSessionRecord, firstCwd). Not the current cwd, which the agent owns.

role.description: core/roles.json's native roles. The old vocabulary (master, orchestrator, session) is translated through core/roles.json's aliases when wezfleet is read, and is never stored.

parent.description: The parent session's sessionId: an edge by identity, never by label. Every one of 20 parents in wezfleet's registry is a session id (census 2026-09-29).

label.description: The short handle: an orchestrator's letter alone (one or two capitals, wezfleet Test-WfLooksLikeOrchestratorLetter), or a subsession's letter and its number within that letter - one to four digits, as wezfleet Split-WfLabel reads it (lib/Allocator.ps1:45), never with a leading zero, because New-WfSessionLabel issues numbers from 1. Recycles by design, so it is a handle, never identity. 17 of 17 labels in the registry have this shape (census 2026-09-30).

origin.description: Who opened the session: fleet when the spawner gave it a fleet session id, else user. The only two values Write-WfSessionRecord writes; registry census: fleet 7, user 24.

fleetSessionId.x-horde-read: W1 fleetSessionId, then W2 fleetSessionId, then W4 sessions[].id, then W3 sessions[].id, then W8 wezfleetSessionId
fleetSessionId.description: The id the run manifest gave this session. wezfleet writes an empty string for none (24 of 31 registry records); here none is absent.

retired.description: A tombstone: the session was closed out. Its record is kept so its label stays held (wezfleet Set-WfSessionFields -Retired).

lastSeen.description: When the session last ran a tool, ISO 8601 in UTC with a Z. wezfleet writes ToUniversalTime().ToString('o'); 77 of 77 registry timestamps have this shape.

runId.description: The run the session belongs to: yyyyMMdd-HHmmss and a slug (wezfleet New-WfRunId, ConvertTo-WfSlug). 194 of 194 run folders have this shape.

labelCycle.description: Which wrap of the label counter issued the label, so a label resolves to one session. wezfleet's claims write -1 for none; here none is absent. Never negative; that is not enforced here, because core/Schema.ps1 implements no minimum keyword.

retiredAt.description: When the session was retired, ISO 8601 in UTC with a Z, as lastSeen.

lastTool.description: The name of the last tool the session ran (Bash, PowerShell, Read, Write in the registry). wezfleet writes an empty string for none (7 of 31); here none is absent.

title.description: The run manifest's title for the session; the manifest defaults it to the session's fleet id (wezfleet lib/Run.ps1).

dependsOn.description: The fleet session ids this session waits for, as the manifest lists them. An empty list is a fact (it waits for none); absent means not recorded. 49 of 49 entries in the rosters are non-empty strings.

spawnedAt.description: When the spawner launched the session, ISO 8601 in UTC with a Z. 306 of 306 roster values have this shape; entries older than the field have none, and absent is never read as fresh.
